title: Nutational Spin Pumping and Dissipation
abstract: At terahertz drive frequencies, magnetization dynamics enter an inertial regime beyond the scope of standard Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) theory. We reveal a nutational damping torque comprising a bulk term and an interfacial contribution that describes spin emission into adjacent metals. The interfacial term generates nutational spin pumping: a dc spin current that scales quadratically with the drive frequency. Using a scattering approach, we relate this effect to microscopic material parameters and predict pronounced enhancements in ultrathin films and low-Fermi-energy conductors. Nutational spin pumping can be detected directly via the inverse spin Hall effect or indirectly via thickness-dependent renormalization of nutational damping.
summary: This theoretical work extends magnetization dynamics theory to the THz regime by incorporating inertial effects into the LLG equation. It predicts a novel nutational spin pumping current that scales quadratically with the drive frequency. The findings offer a microscopic understanding of this effect, which can be detected via the inverse spin Hall effect, advancing spintronic device design.
main_problem: The study addresses magnetization dynamics in the terahertz (THz) regime where standard Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) theory fails due to inertial effects.
main_result: The authors predict a novel nutational spin pumping effect, generating a DC spin current that scales quadratically with the drive frequency ($\omega^2$).
method: The analysis combines extending the LLG equation to include inertial terms with scattering theory applied to FM/NM junctions.
model_or_system: The system involves ferromagnets (FMs) coupled to adjacent metals (NMs), modeled using an inertial extension of the LLG equation and a microscopic Hamiltonian approach.
key_observables: Nutational spin pumping current ($J_{s,z}^{	ext{nsp}}$), resonance frequencies ($\omega_{	ext{prec}}$ and $\omega_{	ext{nut}}$), and the ratio of nutational to conventional spin currents.
important_parameters: Terahertz drive frequencies ($\omega$), Gilbert damping ($\alpha$), and the inertial damping parameter ($\alpha\eta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the linearized regime for small driving fields and utilizes approximations derived from scattering theory expansions in powers of the frequency ($\omega$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the conventional (linear in $\omega$) and nutational (quadratic in $\omega$) spin current contributions. Figure 2 plots the nutational damping strength dependence on material parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the inertial LLG equation, deriving the nutational spin pumping current via macroscopic analysis, and finally calculating this current microscopically using scattering theory in the NM-FM junction.
why_interesting: The inclusion of inertial terms and the resulting frequency-squared dependence of the spin current provides a rich, non-linear extension to standard spin-torque phenomena, relevant for understanding high-frequency spintronics.
